#1538. AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros: Five things we learned – a poor squad picked apart

AC Milan’s Europa League misery continued at San Siro on Thursday night as they were beaten 2-0 by Ferencvaros.

Ruben Amorim made six changes to the team that won the derby against Inter, hoping that the entire group would remain buoyed by that performance to secure a much-needed win in Europe. However, what followed was the worst performance of his tenure so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Lenny Joseph netted twice in the second half to capitalise on errors and fire the Hungarian side to a memorable win. Ferencvaros were not even rocked by a red card to the substitute Yusuf as they kept the Rossoneri at bay quite easily, securing a two-goal win they deserved.

The result means that Milan have now dropped out of even the top 24 spots, and they can just about say goodbye to any hopes of direct last-16 qualification barring a miracle. Ivan Stoev has five things we learned from another dismal midweek game.

It’s difficult to pick five talking points after a game like this, as we can probably spend quite a bit of time discussing how bad each of the players were. But let’s try to address the bigger issue.

This squad is full of sheep, lacking both leaders and the quality to compete. We can talk all about how much Amorim rotates the squad and try to ease the blow by suggesting the Rossoneri didn’t field their best XI. Yet, if the management were serious about making the club competitive, then the rotational players should be above the quality of almost all teams competing in the Europa League, bar a few.

Obviously, if we assume Amorim is the right choice and Gerry Cardinale is serious, then it will take a lot more than a single transfer window and three new players to get Milan to compete on a few fronts, which was further proven against Ferencvaros.

Out of the whole squad, the only player that can change a game is Diego Moreira, who doesn’t play every game and has lots of room for improvement still. Not to mention that playing with the likes of Filippo Terracciano, Ardon Jashari and even Goncalo Ramos is not helping Belgium at all.

The rest of the squad lack either the quality or the mentality. The collective arrogance on the pitch was insufferable to watch, with Ferencvaros looking like the only side that had any desire to actually win. Whilst the Diavolo looked like they were playing a game in the park with no aggression, no focus, no intensity. No nothing.

It’s a bit pointless to discuss individuals because I think the wider point is clear – Milan lack leaders, Milan lack quality and Milan lack a game changer that can get the ball and make something happen when the tough gets going.

It was made evident after four games in the Europa League and a few blunders in Serie A that there’s lots of work to be done in January and next summer.

Again, it’s difficult to pick and choose which player to discuss, but given Ramos is the Rossoneri’s most expensive signing ever, it’s probably fair that the pressure starts mounting on him.

Listen, I wasn’t too bothered by the lack of goals initially, as the striker did well in the build-up and opened up space for his teammates; he also ran a lot in both phases of the game. Let’s also be honest, he has lacked the service to actually get the goal-scoring opportunities.

Nevertheless, in the last few games and especially against Ferencvaros, he has been dire – his build-up is poor, his ball control is pretty bad and when he does get a shot off, it’s usually miles away.

Now, obviously he’s not a striker that’s going to create chances for himself; he lacks the pace and the trickery, which is fine if you are good in the other aspects of the game. However, we can’t keep grasping for straws.

The reality is that the former PSG man is just not living up to the expectations given the hefty sum paid for him in the summer.

In retrospect, maybe it wasn’t wise to spend such a sum on a player who needs quality around him in order to be a better facilitator or to receive more chances overall. The reality as of now is that the Portuguese is a disappointment.

Again, as we said, most players in the squad lack quality or mentality and unfortunately for us there are some that lack both and it’s way past the tipping point at this stage.

Terracciano, for starters, has not shown anything worth mentioning in all of his games with the red and black shirt and there’s really no reason for him to get minutes. Even without pressure, he’s just not of the needed level.

Jashari is another one that the fans and the management have hoped will bounce back after his lengthy injury after joining Milan. Yet, he’s probably had one good game from start to finish and there’s always gaps in his game.

It’s probably wise at this point to accept he’s not going to live up to the expectations and a solution needs to be found on the market, especially given Luka Modric will most likely be retiring at the end of the season.

There are also other players in this category that didn’t necessarily participate in last night’s game but should have the same fate – Pervis Estupinan and Ruben Loftus-Cheek to name a couple.

If nothing else, these poor performances should highlight to the management where the gap in quality is and what the strategy on the transfer market should be.

4. De Winter’s disastrous performance proves costly

I think the biggest individual call-out should definitely be the Belgian, who played an awful back pass to Lorenzo Torriani on the first goal. Yes, the keeper could’ve and should’ve done much better, but that back pass was just so sloppy – it could put an outfield player in a tricky situation, let alone a goalkeeper that perhaps isn’t as comfortable with his feet.

This especially coming from a player who should’ve been a certainty at the back given the heavily rotated squad.

We can also partly criticise the intervention on the second goal, because it started the whole sequence leading to the Joseph’s brace. Yes, it was a bit unlucky where the ball ended up, but you can also argue it was sloppy, the same way you can argue that a keeper clearing the ball into the opponent’s feet after a shot instead of towards the corner is the keeper’s fault to an extent.

It’s just unacceptable to go from bullying Thuram to being bullied by not even Ferencvaros’s first-choice striker.

5. Amorim’s tactics fail, but the players also struggle

I think it’s probably fair to criticise the Portuguese coach a bit too, as the Hungarians totally outplayed the Diavolo at the San Siro and were tactically better. All in all, they had the answer to everything Milan tried to offer on the night.

At the same time, I’m torn to put the blame fully on Ruben Amorim because he did make a triple change at half-time, bringing on Pulisic, Moreira and Gila, which was still at 0-0. At that point, the Rossoneri had more than enough quality on the pitch to be able to deal with whatever Ferencvaros had to offer.

Instead, two individual mistakes gave away the opening goal and it all went downhill from there. Even after the red card, Milan struggled to create a big chance.

I personally struggle to blame this fully on tactics given all the circumstances and we are back to the point that the Milan squad are just not good enough and lacks that killer mentality.

#1537. AC Milan: Diego Moreira is already doing better than Rafael Leão on his debut

Arriving this summer at AC Milan from Strasbourg for around 60 million euros, bonus included, Diego Moreira already justifies the investment made by the Rossoneri. The winger once again stood out during the derby against Inter, with two assists and a superb free kick to contribute to his team’s victory. A remarkable debut which also allows him to gradually forget Rafael Leão, who left to join Galatasaray.

Moreira’s numbers already speak for him. In five starts in all competitions, the Portuguese has scored four goals and provided three assists. In the league, he has the same record in six appearances, including four in the starting XI. For comparison, during his first season in Serie A in 2019-2020, Rafael Leão needed 24 games to reach the four-goal mark.

#1536. Man United 3-2 Roma PLAYER RATINGS: Which star delivered their best performance in a red shirt? Whose physicality is something to marvel at? And who deserves 3/10 for their abysmal defending?

Published: 17:21 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

Manchester United pulled out an enormous win for Michael Carrick as they fought back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 in the Champions League.

Winless in nine games heading into this European night under the lights and United were staring at 10 without a win, a record that was last struck in 1978, when they were two down at half-time after a dreadful start.

But United conjured up spirit that has been barely visible so far this season as a brace from Matheus Cunha - who finished the night getting sent off - followed a penalty from Bruno Fernandes to seal the most crucial of wins.

What it means for Carrick's future in the medium to longer term remains to be seen.

Those upstairs at United have privately taken a lot of the blame and want to end the churn of managers carrying the can for poor player performances. Only time will tell how big a turning point this night can be.

Daily Mail Sport's NATHAN SALT was at Old Trafford on a frantic night to run the rule over the players...

Matheus Cunha rescued victory from the jaws of defeat for Manchester United against Roma

Made a big save low to his right on the stroke of half-time to prevent further embarrassment for United and, as it turned out, give them a fighting chance of getting the result they pulled out of the hat. His distribution seems to have really regressed this season with far too many aimless balls, though.

Made a huge recovery tackle to deny Rodrigo Mora a third and in a feckless first half it was he who bust a gut where others didn't. Yes, it's a low bar but Yoro has actually been one of, if not, the best United performers during this never-ending malaise.

A performance littered with mistakes that, in truth, looked to have been scrubbed from his game coming into this campaign. He's the leader of the back-line and he did everything but lead in a first half that saw positioning and decision-making leave a lot to be desired. His clearance that resulted in Roma's second goal was diabolical. Booked and was fortunate not to have been sent off.

Harry Maguire left a lot to be desired in a defensive performance littered with basic errors

Thrust into the side in place of Lisandro Martinez and his head will have been spinning when he gave away a penalty for a handball, which Donyell Malen converted. Booked for a lunging challenge that is becoming a worrying trend of tackling with studs up. May sound daft but he needs coaching by Jonny Evans or Jonathan Woodgate on a better way to slide tackle. Booked.

Abysmal defending for Roma's first goal as he committed to the attack like a winger and left Matias Soule the freedom of Manchester to score. Kept pushing forward – you have to assume by instruction – and kept being found wanting. Options are slim but he's not making any positive contribution to the team from left back. Needs a stop putting to it.

Got told to 'f**k off' by Bruno Fernandes in a fraught first half for a bobbly pass to tee him up on the edge of the box. Made a couple of smart bursts through lines but he's in the side to protect the defence and he didn't do it. Night cut short when he pulled his hamstring 60 seconds into the second half.

Will be disappointed with himself at how sloppily he gave away the ball in a turnover which exposed his defenders for the first goal. That error aside, he settled in and improved as it wore on. His ability to actually beat a man is in short supply in this United side and his physicality was something to marvel at at times.

Kobbie Mainoo actually looks to drive past players, a skill in short supply at United

Always has a buzz about him when he gets the ball and he was the only one to come back from Como with any crumb of credit. Here it was a more sobering affair where his influence was heavily restricted and it means his wait for a United goal goes on. Not managed one since December 2025.

A night of frustration for large spells but one that did eventually serve up a goal and assist for the United captain. He was unfairly booked when Soule got into a pushing match that was very one sided down in the corner. Missed a second-half penalty (which was re-taken due to encroachment) and made no mistake second time around. All that aside, it was a poor look when he's berating team-mates when his own performance level is way below what he's capable of, mind you.

Comfortably the best player in a United shirt on the night - even with the red card. For one, he gets stuck in. For two, it was Cunha who won the penalty – however fortunate a decision that was – that Fernandes eventually converted to make it 2-1. He deserved an assist when he set Mbeumo free for a run on goal moments later. Scored two crucial late goals that will airbrush just how bad a tackle he made to see red. Could make a case for his best performance in a United shirt. It's up there.

Had his head in his hands, much like a lot of the supporters, when he struck both posts after being played through one v one by Cunha. Had a couple of opportunities to scamper through on goal but just didn't have the pace.

Bryan Mbeumo will want his second half breakaway chance back after striking both posts

Muted in celebration at the end and given everything he's had to navigate this season that's perhaps understandable. But this was a shot in the arm, how big we need to wait and see. People have labelled him a dead man walking but he's not giving up yet.

Youri Tielemans (for Carlos Baleba, 51) - 5

Did OK, but didn't do a great deal to drive the play forward. Not exactly the perfect foil to Mainoo, who is stylistically similar.

Lifted the crowd and helped change the game. Should have won a penalty when he was hacked down and it was his assist to Cunha that sealed victory. Coudln't have made a stronger case to start on Sunday.

Lisandro Martinez (for Ayden Heaven, 75) - 6

The fact he was far away from the eventual headlines was probably a good thing for all concerned after what transpired at Stamford Bridge.

#1535. Alajbegović’s first Serie A goal and Boga sink ten-man Napoli on Juventus’s birthday

Juventus beat Napoli 2-0 at the Allianz Stadium, with both goals arriving after a goalless first half. Luciano Spalletti's side now sit seventh, with Napoli eighth, ahead of a Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar.

A first Serie A goal from a Bosnian teenager and a late curler from a substitute gave Juventus victory over Napoli on Sunday 1 November 2026. The game at the Allianz Stadium was goalless at half-time. It finished 2-0.

The result followed a difficult run. Juventus had won just one of their previous four Serie A games. Their last outing ended in a 0-2 defeat against Genoa. Some home fans jeered the team early in the second half.

Napoli’s own match report described the first hour as balanced, with good chances for both teams, before Juventus took control. Guglielmo Vicario made an excellent early save to keep out a diving header from Lorenzo Lucca. Juan Cabal hit the post before the half-hour mark.

Spalletti changed the game from the bench. Federico Gatti replaced Weston McKennie at the break. Edon Zhegrova came on for Randal Kolo Muani on 59 minutes. The substitute skipped past Rrahmani and laid the ball off to Alajbegović. Alajbegović cut inside and fired a left-footed shot into the far corner beyond Alex Meret.

Napoli were then reduced to ten men. Kelly and Jérémie Boga had replaced Jhon Lucumí and Alajbegović on 72 minutes. Andrea Cambiaso came on for Cabal on 83. He set up Boga, who sealed the win with a right-footed curler three minutes from time.

Sky Sport Italia’s ratings made Alajbegović man of the match and called the win important for keeping Juventus in the race for the European places. Across the full 90 minutes, the match statistics favoured the home side. Juventus had 18 shots to Napoli’s 8, with 4 on target against 1. They also won 13 corners to 4. Possession was almost level, at 49% to 51%.

After ten games, Spalletti’s side have five wins, two draws and three defeats. Lazio lead the table on 28 points after nine wins and a draw.

Primo gol in carriera in Serie A, così. ✨ pic.twitter.com/TTGoL4MMyR

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 1, 2026

It was a second straight league win over Napoli for Juventus, who beat them 3-0 on 25 January 2026. Napoli’s defeat ended a run that included a 4-1 win over Monza. They now face FC Porto away in the Champions League on Wednesday 4 November.

Juventus travel to AZ Alkmaar in the Europa League League Phase on Thursday 5 November, with kick-off at 21:00 CET.

#1534. GdS: €100m at risk for Milan between Champions and Europa League – the breakdown

The ups and downs that AC Milan have experienced so far this season could prove costly in the end, as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport this morning.

Ruben Amorim’s tenure at the club has certainly been a mixed bag so far. While the results in the league have been okay with 21 points after 10 games, they have been the opposite in the Europa League with a mere three points after four games.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

As Gazzetta dello Sport reports this morning (see featured image), the problem isn’t just that Milan are struggling on the pitch, but also that it could have a massive effect on the finances. Between a top-four finish and a Europa League failure, we are talking about €100m.

Starting with the present, Milan have collected a mere €14.6m from the Europa League so far, excluding ticket sales for the games against Benfica and Ferencvaros. In other words, it’s just the guaranteed revenue plus the prize money for a win (€450k).

Direct qualification to the knockout phase, which was definitely the goal at the start, has now become rather difficult. Not even winning all of the remaining four games would be a guarantee, as that would take Milan to 15 points, and 16 might be required.

The feeling is that Milan have to focus on reaching the knockout play-offs instead. If they were to fail even with that, as the pink newspaper continues, we would be talking about a loss of €8m for the round of 16, between prize money and ticket sales.

Looking at the bigger picture, given that the Rossoneri among the favourites to win the competition in the summer, doing so would generate total revenue of €40m. Furthermore, lifting the trophy would secure qualification to the Champions League.

After missing the last two editions, failing to qualify yet again would be a massive failure for the entire RedBird project. This is especially true as the 2027-28 season will mark the beginning of a new cycle for UEFA in terms of commercial and TV rights, with numbers expected to significantly increase.

According to the newspaper, the total pot of prize money for the participating clubs will increase from the current €2.46bn to €2.8bn. For the Rossoneri, this would mean going from a minimum revenue of around €40m to around €50m, even before stepping onto the pitch.

To this figure, one must add around €10-15m from the ticket sales, so failure to qualify for the competition next season would mean missing out on a minimum of €60m (!). It could quickly rise to €70-80m too, so we really are talking about a lot.

Qualifying for the Champions League would increase the overall revenue by more than 20% and fuel Milan’s project of growth, especially since other improvements are on the cards too. For example, from 2028-39, Adidas will start paying €50m per season to the club.

#1533. Michael Carrick might STILL be one game from the sack. A one-night stand of epic proportions was up there with Man United's best but produced more questions than answers, writes CHRIS WHEELER

Published: 02:31 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 11:18 EDT, 4 November 2026

What a crazy, chaotic and, frankly, confusing night this was at Old Trafford. The grand old place has seen a few of them down the years, and Manchester United's incredible comeback win over Roma was right up there with the best.

By the end of it, the fans were loving United and hating the Glazers in keeping with their doctrine. Michael Carrick was savouring arguably his greatest moment as head coach, and yet might still be one game from the sack. Two-goal hero Matheus Cunha was being manhandled off the pitch and towards the tunnel, furious at not being able to celebrate with his teammates.

For Carrick, this felt like the equivalent of Erik ten Hag's win over Manchester City in the 2024 FA Cup final and Ruben Amorim's incredible 4-3 victory over Lyon in the Europa League quarter-final last year. The feelgood factor and sense of elation around Old Trafford was palpable.

Neither of those wins were enough to keep Ten Hag and Amorim in a job for much longer, and that is the conundrum for United bosses this morning.

If the feeling in the boardroom – and it remains an if – is to relieve Carrick of his duties, can they be swayed by a one-night stand, albeit one of epic proportions.

If United can follow this up with victory on Sunday over Aston Villa and Unai Emery – one of the candidates being touted as Carrick's replacement – can they really sack their head coach at the start of the international break?

Michael Carrick gave his players the half-time fire power needed to pull off a famous fightback

More than just pulling off the much-needed win against Roma, it felt as if his stars were playing for their manager

On another night when United fans turned on the Glazers, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, director of football Jason Wilcox and even the players as boos greeted the half-time whistle and the 'play like you mean it' banner made a re-appearance for the first time in three years, it was a reminder that the most popular person at the club might be the man who is about to get the bullet.

The players certainly looked as though they are playing for Carrick, and afterwards Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans both gave him their backing.

Looking ahead to this game, Carrick had said: 'Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.'

Those words came true in spectacular fashion. For a while, it felt as though he wouldn't even survive until the Villa game as United's defence fell apart and Roma set a new record for a European opponent taking a two-goal lead at Old Trafford. It could have been worse.

Carrick got his players together at half-time and reminded them that it only takes one moment to light the touchpaper here. 'I don't like talking to the lads too much about the history of this place, but it's magical,' he said. 'There's something when we have these nights and we do it the hard way, and one moment can flip the whole feeling.'

Kobbie Mainoo put it more bluntly. 'We needed a bit of a kick,' said the United midfielder.

It worked. United roared back at Roma, showing a resolve and strength of character that has been missing for much of this season. Fernandes converted a retaken penalty, Cunha levelled and then smashed home the winner late on to give United their first victory in 10 games.

The Brazilian's sending-off for removing his shirt after scoring the third and then committing a silly foul on Leonardo Balerdi meant he wasn't allowed to go on the pitch at the end, much to his indignation. Carrick and his staff were there to reinforce the point.

Results clearly haven't been good enough this season, but one of the criticisms levelled at Carrick is that performances have been even worse. The combination of those two factors have left him fighting to save his job.

On the flip side, it felt like this win and the nature of it counted double. One that raised the roof at Old Trafford and lifted the soul.

Yet for so long on Tuesday night, the mood among the United faithful was one of mutiny. They revived the anti-Glazer campaign by bringing green and gold balloons into the Stretford End, and let them loose as the two teams walked out.

Rather like the protests against the absent owners who keep a safe distance thousands of miles away in America, they were never going to hit their target by reaching the pitch and floated harmlessly into the night air. A barrage of tennis balls had greater impact, but they too were soon cleared out of sight.

Chants against the Glazers, Ratcliffe and Wilcox rang out long before kick-off. 'You can stick your new stadium up your a***' chanted the fans. The game was seconds old when we heard the first rendition of 'sell United and f*** off home' followed by the tribute song to Carrick.

Even at a critical point in the game when VAR was studying Gianluca Mancini's challenge on Cunha to see if it warranted a penalty, the United fans broke into a chorus of 'we want Glazers out'. It was the same after Cunha fired the decisive goal as supporters turned on the Americans and voiced their support for Carrick once more. They were caught between wanting to vent their anger at the owners and back Carrick and the team.

Fervent and continuing protests against the ownership underscored Carrick's own popularity, despite being potentially days from getting the sack

Matheus Cunha might have been the late hero but he was unable to celebrate with his team-mates and manager after taking off his shirt

'The players one hundred per cent feed off the crowd, absolutely no doubt whatsoever,' said Carrick. 'I understand there's frustration and disappointment, I totally get that.

'Probably the time when it was easy for them not to be there, they were there. I felt that there was frustration, of course there was. I get it. But I know what they're like and we've got to give them something to go on.'

United managed to do that in the end, but it was a funny sort of night. One that produced more questions than answers. The biggest of them concerns Carrick. Is he doing enough to convince his employers that United can turn a corner? Victory in Europe doesn't alter the fact they are one place above the Premier League relegation zone.

There is one more game against Villa and then the choice is very simple: stick or twist?

#1532. Atlético de Madrid: Diego Simeone reacts to Julián Álvarez’s apology

Diego Simeone reacted with satisfaction to the apologies presented by Julián Álvarez after the Argentine striker’s statements about his future and his interest in FC Barcelona. The Atlético de Madrid coach welcomed his player’s approach, believing that it took courage to recognize his wrongs. “I have a lot of respect for people who apologize, because asking for forgiveness is not easy. I am happy for Julián. He will feel much more at peace now. When he says something like that, it’s because he sincerely means it.”declared the Madrid technician.

Simeone also recalled the importance of his striker for the ambitions of the Colchoneros, while Julián Álvarez recently admitted that he would have understood the anger of the supporters after having mentioned a possible departure. “We need him. If the club is to reach the heights that fans dream of, we need Julián to be at his best.”insisted the coach. Words which testify to his desire to turn the page and place the Argentinian at the heart of the Madrid project, despite the tensions aroused by his declarations this summer.

#1531. McKennie ruled out of AZ trip with adductor fatigue as Alajbegović and Cabal return

Weston McKennie will miss Thursday's Europa League game at AZ Alkmaar with fatigue in his right adductor, though he has no muscle tear. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal are fit again, a relief for a badly stretched squad before a demanding trip.

Juventus will travel to AZ Alkmaar without Weston McKennie. The American has fatigue in his adductor and will sit out Thursday’s Europa League match. The news is not all bad. Kerim Alajbegović and Juan Cabal, who also came off in the 2-0 win over Napoli, have both been cleared.

McKennie lasted only the first half at the Allianz Stadium. Federico Gatti replaced him at the break. Luciano Spalletti had to send on an extra defender because McKennie felt a pull in his adductor. The coach also had few other players to choose from.

A short rest should be enough, because the injury is fatigue rather than a tear, Sky Sport Italia reported. He should be back for the league. The problem is in his right adductor. The medical staff will check him again before Thursday, ANSA said.

Alajbegović had both a goal and a scare against Napoli. He opened the scoring in the 70th minute and was replaced by Jérémie Boga two minutes later. Boga then added the second in the 87th. At 19 years and 41 days, the teenager has set a new mark: no non-Italian scorer in a Serie A meeting of these two clubs has been younger.

His knee knock has already cleared up. Cabal made way for Andrea Cambiaso after 83 minutes with cramp. That is put down to him not having started a game for some time. He will be available in Alkmaar.

Their return matters because the squad is badly stretched. Seven players are on the long-term injury list. Rugani, Zhegrova, Ekhator and Milik were left out of the UEFA squad. Losing McKennie, who can play several positions, leaves Spalletti with even fewer options for the trip to the Netherlands.

The match at AZ kicks off at 21:00 CET on 5 November. It is Matchday 4 of the league phase. Juventus have two wins and a draw so far.

AZ will be hard to break down at home. Their last home defeat in Europe was 4-1 to Aston Villa in the Conference League in October 2023.

Juventus arrive in good scoring form. They have nine goals in this season’s Europa League. Only Benfica, with ten, have scored more. That is Juventus’s best total after three games of a European campaign since 1999/2000.

⚪⚫ Kerim Alajbegović's first league goal for Juventus ✅#UEL | @juventusfc pic.twitter.com/GPcn8KJZga

— UEFA Europa League (@EuropaLeague) November 2, 2026

History against Dutch opposition also offers encouragement. Juventus are unbeaten in three previous Europa League games against Dutch clubs, with two wins and one draw. They scored seven goals and conceded one in those matches.

McKennie’s absence will shape the midfield in Alkmaar, but the focus will quickly shift to his recovery. His place for the next league game is in doubt. Juventus visit Fiorentina on Matchday 11, on Sunday 8 November 2026 at 20:45.

#1527. Unai Emery has closed gap between Aston Villa and Europe's elite - but rampant Barcelona proved there is still a way to go as Lamine Yamal dazzles, writes OLIVER HOLT

Published: 17:17 EDT, 3 November 2026 | Updated: 11:27 EDT, 4 November 2026

John McGinn heard the question. His eyes darted around Barcelona's packed media auditorium for a second or two on Monday night. What was it like to be about to play in the Nou Camp, the Aston Villa skipper had been asked, as if this were to be some sort of spin off from Bill and Ted's Excellent Adventure.

McGinn was careful with his answer. He did not seek to downplay the nature of the occasion or the thrill that comes with lining up in such a majestic arena. But he was determined not to play the wide-eyed ingenu. 'What our club is trying to do now,' McGinn said, 'is make this normal, make this a yearly experience.'

So when he and his team-mates walked up the flight of steps from the dressing rooms into the vast bowl of the stadium on Tuesday evening, they were here to show that they were not arrivistes. Villa is a historic club. They won this competition in 1982, ten years before Barcelona ever did. They were not here for a treat or to get patted on the back just for turning up.

It is nearly 20 years since Liverpool became the last English club to win here and nobody gave Villa too much chance of ending that drought. They are being told constantly that the odds are stacked against them and that their much-admired manager, Unai Emery, may be tempted by the entreaties of struggling 'giants' elsewhere.

That was the reason why this game early in the league phase had attained so much importance. For Villa, it was a symbol of something they aspire to. They want to get used to belonging in this company, to walking up those steps, to emerging into the stadium in the pouring rain, and staring at players of the calibre of Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsi staring back at them.

It still feels as if they stand on the cusp of something bigger but they blew their shot at proving that on Tuesday night. They needed to be at their best to have a chance of beating Hansi Flick's side, which sits atop LaLiga, and they were far too naïve in defence to get close to causing a shock. They are rising but this was a step too far at this stage of their evolution.

Lamine Yamal (centre) and Barcelona had plenty to smile about after beating Aston Villa 3-0

Yamal opened the scoring for Barcelona after just seven minutes with this left-footed finish

Raphinha (right) doubled Barca's lead after half-time with this strike at the Spotify Nou Camp

The Nou Camp, which is still in the midst of an extensive renovation and was only about two-thirds full, was ringed by towering yellow cranes, peering down at the floodlit patch of green. From their lofty vantage point, they saw Villa get off to the worst possible start.

Only seven minutes had gone when Emery's team gift-wrapped a present for the home side. Zion Suzuki played the ball out short to Joao Gomes but Gomes panicked under pressure from the Barcelona press and the close attention of Pedri. He played the ball square without looking, straight to Yamal.

Of all the players he could have found, Gomes had to find Yamal. The Spain superstar squared up Pau Torres and then curled the ball around him with a gentle caress of his left boot. Suzuki was helpless. The ball nestled in the corner of the net. Barcelona had scored 56 goals in 14 games before this match. Extending the hand of generosity to them must have felt particularly galling for Emery.

Villa almost hit back immediately. A stinging volley from Matty Cash was deflected wide and Barcelona looked jittery at the back. Nicolas Jackson played a square ball to Johan Manzambi, who should have equalised but scuffed his first-time effort wide of Joan Garcia. Barcelona were thankful for Garcia's intervention when he raced out of his goal to dispossess Jackson as he charged on to a through ball.

Yamal was rampant. His battle with Ian Maatsen was a mismatch and Maatsen was booked after 11 minutes for hacking him down. Villa were still intent on playing themselves into trouble. Suzuki repeated his mistake when he tried to play the ball out to Joao Gomes. This time, Pedri beat him to it and the loose ball fell to Gordon. Gordon hit his shot towards the corner but Suzuki redeemed himself by diving to push it away.

Barcelona had the better of the play. They looked like scoring every time they went forward. Time and again, either Raphinha or Yamal found space to run at the Villa defence, which was barely coping. Even in that context, though, it was an open game. Villa had chances, too. Manzambi forced a fine save out of Garcia. A Jackson breakaway was thwarted by a last-ditch block.

But seven minutes after the break, Barcelona doubled their lead. Fermin Lopez played a clever ball to Raphinha, who had found a yard of space in the box. Raphinha, LaLiga's leading scorer this season, drilled a left-foot shot goalwards and it deflected off the heel of Torres, wrong-footed Suzuki and rolled over the line.

Barcelona put the game out of reach midway through the half when Joao Cancelo forced his way past McGinn on the left flank and hit a sumptuous cross into the box with the outside of his right foot. Raphinha gambled on the path of the ball, darted behind his marker and tucked the ball away.

Raphinha completed the scoreline with this cute finish as Barcelona completed their victory

For Aston Villa, this will be a learning curve as they look to go far in the Champions League

Villa manager Unai Emery will have plenty to think about after another Nou Camp defeat

Substitute Leon Goretzka hit the face of a post for Villa late on but the game was already gone. There was no shame in losing to a team who are one of the favourites to win the competition this season but there was frustration in the way Villa had handed their opponents the advantage.

Emery looked bedraggled as he stood on the touchline in the rain, arms folded, shaking his head. This was his 15th defeat in 16 visits to the Nou Camp. As Villa's coach fights to edge his team closer to the elite of the game, this game will become just one more bad memory.

#1525. Juventus extend Elimoghale to 2029 as Carnevali puts youth sector at the centre

Juventus have tied academy forward Destiny Elimoghale to the club until 30 June 2029, on the day Giovanni Carnevali spoke to shareholders about the youth sector. The 2009-born striker has already been named in a European squad while injuries stretch the first team.

The club announced Elimoghale’s renewal on 3 November. That was the same day chief executive Giovanni Carnevali addressed shareholders at the Allianz Stadium. He called for a single project covering the first team, the Next Gen and the youth sector.

Elimoghale has come through every level of the club’s academy. He has been at Juventus since childhood. This season he began playing professional football in Serie C.

The NEC fixture was the opening matchday of the Europa League league phase. Spalletti named three Next Gen players because the first team was hit by injuries, Tuttosport reported. Pagnucco and Owusu joined Elimoghale. All three were in a European squad for the first time.

Elimoghale did not get on the pitch in the comfortable win. He stayed on the bench as an unused substitute, alongside Vicario, Pinsoglio and Pagnucco.

Back in Serie C, his minutes have been mixed. In a 5-3 home defeat to Albinoleffe on the sixth matchday, he tried two long-range shots. One went just wide. Goalkeeper Baldi saved the other. At Trento on the 11th matchday, he replaced Leone in the 70th minute of a 2-1 defeat. The match came in Serie C Group A. He was among Massimo Brambilla’s unused substitutes in the 1-1 home draw with Pro Vercelli on 2 November. That matchday 12 fixture was the Next Gen’s most recent game.

Carnevali said the club must bring its youth sector back to the level of recent years. He added that Juventus must keep trying to improve it. Securing a home-grown forward for the long term is consistent with that message.

Carnevali confirmed a change to the UEFA squad list as well, with Ekhator replacing Locatelli.

Aggiornamento della lista UEFA: Jeff Ekhator subentra a Manuel Locatelli. pic.twitter.com/I3Mi1W0PSB

— JuventusFC (@juventusfc) November 3, 2026

For Elimoghale, the wider picture is a first team still short of bodies. Coaches have already turned to the Next Gen once in Europe. A new long-term deal means the club has secured one of those options.

The squad remains stretched heading into the next round of European fixtures. McKennie is suffering from muscle fatigue and will miss the Europa League trip to AZ Alkmaar. Alajbegovic and Cabal are expected to be available in the Netherlands. The trip comes with the European squad list already being reshaped.

#1524. Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season

Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

Their offensive problems tend to come when opponents sit in and ask to be broken down. Hull City, of course, proved as much last weekend when United looked desperately short of ideas in attack.

But you would probably bet on Carrick being more likely to find solutions to that particular conundrum than some of the defensive headaches that again reared their head here.

A week after that shock 2-0 defeat to Hull, United were given another scare when Ipswich took advantage of more meek defending to lead and could easily have scored more in that first half.

With a couple of days of the transfer window still remaining, it would feel remiss of United not to add a quality left-back before the deadline passes.

Those 15 minutes in the first half when Abdul Fatawu gave Luke Shaw a torrid time, not least in that moment he raced away from the United defender to cross for Leif Davis to score, should tell United’s hierarchy everything about the risks of not reinforcing in the position.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Defensive rebuilding is next summer’s big project but some things cannot wait and that is before we get to some of the issues in the other full-back position, which Ipswich also exploited. Fatawu aside, Daizen Maeda and Davis caused Diogo Dalot and Mbeumo problems down United’s right and the excellent Julio Enciso was a persistent nuisance until the game fell away from Ipswich.

For all the defensive concerns, though, United were exhilarating going forward, especially once they found themselves in front after benefiting from a curious ruling that dictated Harry Maguire’s “accidental” handball in the lead-up to the home team’s second goal was “not punishable” because he did not end up scoring.

In other words, had Maguire himself found the net and not seen his cross-cum-shot deflect in off the Ipswich defender Jacob Greaves, the goal would not have stood.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

United were brilliant from that point on. There had been flashes of the threat they hold in the opening 45 minutes but thereafter Ipswich just found themselves routinely bludgeoned and unable to escape the tailspin. As the rain poured down, the goals poured in. Gary O’Neil, the Ipswich manager, talked about a lack of “emotional discipline” but plenty of teams would have found United hard to contain in that moment.

Rashford was a threat on his first start for United for 626 days. Harness his talent in the right way and he will be an enormous asset. Cunha’s withdrawn role, with Fernandes and Mbeumo routinely racing in behind United’s false nine, caused Ipswich no end of problems. Amad Diallo and Mason Mount were missing through injury and Benjamin Sesko, a substitute, is still working his way back to fitness after missing all of pre-season. Patrick Dorgu almost scored a couple after coming on. So Carrick has plenty of options.

Fernandes was at his irrepressible best, initially punishing poor Marcelino Núñez after his slip allowed Cunha to play in the United captain to equalise five minutes before the restart and then taking the game away from Ipswich in the second.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

After missing two penalties in pre-season, he made no mistake from the spot after Greaves had brought down Cunha. He then steered home a close-range finish after Mbeumo’s shot was blocked and almost lobbed the Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen from 60 yards. His last act was to send Mbeumo through to score with a delicious lob.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

This was the first time United had scored five goals in a Premier League game since beating Leeds United five years ago and you had to go back 10 years to find the last time they had more shots in a league match.

“There was a good mixture [in attack] there,” Carrick said. “Obviously we’ve got to find the right balance and options. We can play slightly different ways across the front line and a lot of the front players can play different roles.

“It was a little bit different today playing Cunha a bit deeper, and Bryan and Marcus a little bit higher. So it’s up to us to try and get that balance right, but certainly there’s creation and there’s goals within the squad, for sure.”

There was little doubt United benefited from the return of Mainoo in midfield. Summer signing Andrey Santos was the one to make way and Mainoo in turn produced the kind of intelligent, inventive display alongside Youri Tielemans that makes you wonder how Thomas Tuchel did not give the midfielder a minute for England at this summer’s World Cup.

He recycles possession beautifully, excels in the tight spaces, has a nose for goal and an eye for a pass and a lovely ability to glide past players even though he is not quick. Ipswich could not live with him.

Asked where Mainoo could still develop, Carrick said, half in jest: “On today’s performance, not much, really. I thought he was pretty much all-around, very, very good for a first start back. I understand Bruno will get a lot of credit today, and he deserves that as well, but I thought Kobbie was immense in the middle of the pitch for us and underpinned the performance of the team.”

The Man Utd head coach told Sky Sports: “It was a good win. It was a really good win in the end. We played some really good football. The biggest thing today was the mentality of the boys tp overcomes setbacks. We’re going to have them and it depends on how you deal with them. I was really pleased with that. It’s easy to look at the result but the mentality and the stubbornness really pleased me.

“We controlled the game pretty well for the most part. A lot of our play was looking on the way to how we wanted it to look. The boys took it on really well and we were fabulous.”

And on Bruno Fernandes, Carrick added: “He showed his quality today. Bruno did what he’s good at. He’s had a big week winning awards. Three goals and a fantastic performance.

“There were a lot of positives with and without the ball but it’s the whole mentality dealing with it and trusting each other. Last week didn’t go for us and we accept that. Today was a lot better.

“We’re not getting carried away. We were down last week but everything wasn’t wrong. We can still get better, we haven’t cracked it. We’ll get ready for the next.”

Speaking with Sky Sports, he said: “Really unlucky to be 2-1 down, really unlucky - two of the most unlucky goals you will see, but then not good enough to get back into it. We got punished by a very good side.

“To beat Manchester United at Old Trafford you need the moments to go in your favour and they didn’t. Rules can go against you, or a deflection, there are lots of things that can happen in a game that are beyond your control.

“It is a complicated rule - handball if it’s the goal scorer but not if it takes a deflection and was heading off the target. I think that is tough for a referee.

“But no problem. I’m not here to moan about refs. We get no points, at Old Trafford a lot of people leave with no points but we leave with an understanding of where to get better.

“We have three points from two tough games. A good start for us. It is the Premier League, the lads understand there will be highs and lows. We don’t want there to be too many lows but the lads are fine in there. They understand.”

"I understand the rules, but it doesn't feel right" Ashley Young and Darren Bent react to the reasoning behind Harry Maguire's potential handball not being given 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/MGJdBNhbYx

"We deserved that little bit of luck"Harry Maguire discusses Manchester United's controversial second goal where he appeared to handle the ball 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/AY3vWRCxZZ

The hat-trick hero told Sky Sports: “It was a massive result for us. We lost three points last week. First game at home, the fans have been waiting for this. It’s not to make up for last week, you can’t get six points from it. Second half we were very good.

“Scoring before half-time is always important if it’s to get on top of the game or draw the game. We were in control of the game. In the second half, we were very good.

“Scoring goals is the best feeling in football. Doing a half-time at home with our fans is something I’m proud of. I hope I can do much more and help my team-mate score goals too.”

Mission accomplished, boss 👏 https://t.co/0BGBtMYg3H pic.twitter.com/dN0DayO283

Bruno Fernandes brilliance 🌟🌟🌟 pic.twitter.com/96LiCipQKk

Fernandes stars with a second-half hat-trick as Man Utd eventually cruise to an emphatic victory over newly-promoted Ipswich at Old Trafford.

Bruno Fernandes' hat-trick inspires Man Utd to their first win of the season 👏 pic.twitter.com/GNhpUwFUkV

Dorgu looks hungry for a goal as he fires a thunderbolt towards Scherpen’s near post. The Ipswich goalkeeper is up to the task and bats the shot away for a corner.

Man Utd counter as Lammens throws the ball out to Dorgu, who has acres of space to exploit. He tries to pick out Sesko with a cross, but overhits the delivery by some distance. Man Utd look like they could score every time they venture forward.

The Argentine defender won’t want to see this back again... Enciso puts Martinez under pressure and pinches the ball off him. The Ipswich playmaker then sprints towards Lammens and unselfishly slides a pass into Akpom, who slots the ball into an empty net.

There will be eight minutes of added time to end this game.

Man Utd are pushing for a sixth goal and come scarily close to it, but Dorgo’s close-range header is parried away by Scherpen.

Five-star Man Utd are ripping Ipswich apart again. He didn’t score it, but Fernandes is at the heart of this goal. The playmaker floats a delightful ball over Ipswich’s defence for Mbeumo to chase. The forward beats Scherpen to it and lobs the Ipswich goalkeeper. As the ball bounces towards the goal, it kisses the underside of the crossbar. Despite Greaves’ best efforts, he can’t stop the ball from crossing the line.

Carrick orders a triple change as the rain begins to hammer down at Old Trafford. Cunha, Mainoo and Rashford depart for Sesko, Andrey Santos and Dorgu.

Man Utd are close to a fifth goal, but Cunha is denied by Scherpen at his near post. Just before that, Rashford showcased some exceptional skill and nutmegged Diop, but he couldn’t quite get a shot away.

After a flurry of changes for Ipswich amid the chaos, they’ve switched to a back five. Nunez, Lukic and Maeda are all off, with Palacios, Ouattara and Furlong on as the replacements. For Man Utd, Dalot and Shaw are withdrawn for Yoro and Mazraoui.

Fernandes is overflowing with confidence and attempts to lob Scherpen from near the half-way line. His cheeky attempt shaves the roof of the net.

Mbeumo’s blocked effort kindly falls into Fernandes’ path and once again, the Man Utd displays unerring compsure to calmly slide the ball into the bottom corner from close range, leaving Scherpen with no chance. Man Utd are in cruise control now.

"He's the prince of this place!"Bruno Fernandes completes his hat-trick 🎩 pic.twitter.com/KgLlaMcKGR

Rashford meets a clipped cross, but on this occasion, Scherpen is there to make a strong save.

The Portuguese playmaker is the most composed man in Old Trafford. Fernandes coolly sends Scherpen the wrong way and Man Utd now have an invaluable two-goal advantage.

Bruno Fernandes makes it 3-1 to Manchester United from the spot 🎯 pic.twitter.com/vFh7moSSpb

What a nightmare couple of minutes for Ipswich. Mainoo threads a pass through to Cunha, who is cynically apprehended by Greaves’ sliding challenge. It’s all unravelled for Ipswich. It’s a stonewall penalty. Fernandes will take it.

Wave after wave of Man Utd pressure has finally paid off. Man Utd have Ipswich trapped inside their own half as Akpom attempts to chip the ball over Maguire, who blocks it. The defender strides forward and shoots. It’s heading wide, but takes a wicked deflection off Greaves to nestle in the bottom corner. The goal stands after a VAR check.

Harry Maguire's shot cannons in off Jacob Greaves and Manchester United are in front at Old Trafford after a VAR review! 💪 pic.twitter.com/hUdogDQX6k

Some confusion to clear up following the VAR check. The ball struck Maguire’s hand before he shot, but his deflected effort stands because the Man Utd defender wasn’t deemed the ‘immediate goalscorer’ given Greaves’ intervention.

#MUNIPS – 56'The referee's call of goal for Manchester United was checked and confirmed by VAR – with it deemed that Maguire was not the immediate goalscorer after an accidental handball.VAR: "It's an own goal and the accidental handball is not punishable, so we recommend you…

When it’s not your day ... Mbeumo struggled badly offensively and defensively today and that miss from point blank range summed up his afternoon. Plenty of time yet to turn it around of course but he’s got to step it up.

How has that not gone in?! Dalot whips a deep delivery into the box and Rashford does magnificently to keep it in play, volleying the ball back across goal out of Scherpen’s reach. Mbeumo is about a metre from the goal-line and directs Rashford’s assist onto the bar. It’s an extraordinary miss.

"HOW has he missed?!" Bryan Mbeumo misses a golden opportunity to put Man Utd in front 😬 pic.twitter.com/bnZZswysJa

Enciso skips away from Mainoo and drives at Man Utd’s defence. From incredibly far out, he tries his luck, but fires his shot over the bar. Enciso has been a joy to watch so far today.

Enciso showcases some exquisite skill, pirouetting away from Cunha, who brings down the Ipswich playmaker.

We are back under way for the second half. Man Utd are unchanged at the break, while Ipswich have made an alteration, with Akpom on for Emersonn.

Ipswich have looked very useful going forward and richly deserved their opening goal. Fatawu’s dazzling run was rewarded by Davis’ composed finish, but the visitors’ lead didn’t last long. Nunez’s slip proved costly, with Cunha and Fernandes combining to devastating effect, hauling Man Utd level.

A frantic first half comes to a close. It’s been a thoroughly entertaining game of football so far, with Davis and Fernandes both netting via top-quality finishes.

End-to-end stuff at Old Trafford 🤯Leif Davies got the opening goal for Ipswich before Bruno Fernandes equalised for Man Utd. pic.twitter.com/6TAer5eiGJ

There will be two added minutes at the end of this half. Man Utd are pushing for another goal. Can they find a second before the break?

A timely bit of good fortune for United. Cunha takes advantage of poor Nunez’s slip to play an inch perfect pass in behind for the rampaging Fernandes to race clear and fire home.

Disaster for Nunez... Ipswich have a lot of players up the pitch following a long throw-in and the ball is played back to Nunez. The midfielder slips, gifting the hosts a counter attack. Cunha pounces and slides an inch-perfect pass through to the onrushing Fernandes. The Man Utd captain then fires a thunderous effort in at Scherpen’s near post. It’s a magnificent strike. The Ipswich goalkeeper has no chance of saving that. Nunez looks absolutely gutted.

Bruno Fernandes equalises for Manchester United! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/CdEI1REeUD

Fatawu receives a yellow card for clattering into Mbeumo. This game is being played at breakneck speed.

You would have expected Man Utd to come bursting out of the blocks following last week’s disappointment against Hull, but it’s been a really underwhelming display from the hosts so far. Ipswich deserve their lead.

Ipswich nearly make it two! It’s the same combination for Ipswich as Fatawu floats a deep cross into the box for Davis, who makes a late run. Davis meets the delivery from close range, but doesn’t get a clean connection on the strike, allowing Lammens to tip his effort over the bar.

If the first half an hour or so here has done anything, it’s underline how much United need upgrades and reinforcements at full-back. United are in the market for a left back before the window closes and the way Shaw jumped in and then was done by Fatawu for the goal may see those efforts intensified. Davis was criminally unmarked in the middle (what a finish, though, allowing the ball to come across his body then side foot in) with Mbeumo nowhere.

And United haven’t learned from it. Moments later and Fatawu clips in a cross - with not nearly enough pressure from Shaw to shut it out - and Davis is again unmarked at the back with Dalot occupied and Mbeumo ball watching. United are having a real wobble here. Ipswich have been superb. Gary O’Neil will be loving what he is seeing from his side - they’re brave, aggressive and playing with pace and lots of incisive movement.

What a goal from Davis! Fatawu nutmegs Shaw and then outpaces the Man Utd defender. He reaches the byline and picks out the arriving Davis with a pinpoint. Ipswich’s left back then applies a superb finish, directing a superb half-volley in off the bar.

Ipswich STUN Old Trafford! Leif Davis does superbly to volley past Senne Lammens and give Gary O'Neil's side the lead 💥 pic.twitter.com/sJ0XNf8OiT

Mbeumo floats a deep cross towards Rashford at the back post. The Englishman reaches it, but given the power on the delivery, he can’t quite keep it in play.

Man Utd win another free-kick in presentable territory. On this occasion, Fernandes curls his strike into the Ipswich wall.

Davis threads a clever pass trough to Maeda, who creeps in behind Dalot. The winger bursts into the penalty area, before arrowing a powerful attempt towards the far post, but Lammens is there to make a pivotal stop. Ipswich have looked dangerous going forward.

There’s space in behind Diogo Dalot that Ipswich have again exploited, this time with a fine Leif Davis ball for Daizen Maeda to surge in behind the United right back and force a second big save from Lammens. United look a threat going forward but then so do Ipswich, who are picking their moments to break and doing so well.

Rashford tries his luck from long range with a knuckle-ball free-kick. He doesn’t get any accuracy on the strike and it harmlessly flies off target.

This game has exploded into life in the last couple of minutes. End to end action. Scherpen first denying Dalot, then Ipswich going straight down the other end from a long punted clearance and Enciso, holding off Shaw and Mbeumo, forcing a save from Lammens. In keeping with the basketball nature of things, United then went back up the other end, with Cunha overhitting a cross for the onrushing Rashford before Fernandes’ goalbound shot is blocked. It’s certainly entertaining.

Chances at both ends! Firstly, Emersonn hacks Man Utd’s corner away, and Enciso uses his blistering speed to outpace Shaw and Mbeumo, creating a one-on-one with Lammens, who does excellently to smother the shot. Then Man Utd then fly forward straight away and Cunha fires a low delivery across the six-yard box which is marginally out of Rashford’s reach.

Man Utd counter as Fernandes releases Mbeumo with a ball over the top. The hosts recycle the ball well after Rashford crosses, allowing Dalot to cut in or his left foot and bend a curler for the far corner. Scherpen uses every inch of his towering frame to make an eye-catching diving save.

Maeda shows a great turn of pace to breeze past Mbeumo and reach the byline. Under pressure from Dalot, the winger hits his near post cross into Lammens’ hands.

Again, Rashford runs at Ipswich’s backline and cuts inside to reach the penalty area. He tees up Cunha, who smashes an effort well over the bar.

Martinez attempts an ambitious switch of play, aiming for Maguire, but boots the ball straight out of play. O’Shea and Shaw then both go up for a header, with the Ipswich man coming off worse and staying on the ground. He’s back on his feet now and play resumes.

There’s an early roar from the Old Trafford crowd as Rashford gets on the ball and sprints at Ipswich captain O’Shea, who is playing at right back.

Old Trafford welcomes both sides. Can Man Utd find their first win of the Premier League season or will Ipswich spoil the party?

Carlos Baleba has walking out on to the pitch after being introduced at Old Trafford. The new £70m signing from Brighton has been posing for pictures with a shirt and applauding all sections of the ground. He won’t be in action for another two or three weeks most likely owing to an existing ankle injury.

Carlos Baleba is introduced to the Manchester United fans! 👋 pic.twitter.com/QHTCkpe5dz

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a recap of both line-ups.

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

"He's a fantastic footballer." Ashley Young discusses Marcus Rashford 🔊 pic.twitter.com/4hYAtx9zZF

Michael Carrick explains the changes to his Man Utd starting XI to face Ipswich 🔴Watch the game live: https://t.co/0AejI4B8dF pic.twitter.com/p9FD36h3OM

Against Hull, Man Utd’s forward line looked way off the pace. In an attempt to stop history repeating itself, Michael Carrick has turned to Marcus Rashford, who is making his first start for the club since the end of 2024.

When Rashford last featured for Man Utd, he was wearing the No.10 shirt. That is now occupied by Mathues Cunha who starts as the central frontman, with Rashford now sporting the No.9.

The hosts will also need captain Bruno Fernandes to deliver. He will levels below his exceptionally high standards last time out, while Bryan Mbeumo also needs to make more of an impact.

It was short and not sweet. Playing in their first top-flight campaign since 2001-02, Ipswich finished 19th with just 22 points under Kieran McKenna.

This time, Gary O’Neil is the boss and they’ve already ticked off one victory thanks to those three points against Sunderland.

Is he the man to guide Ipswich to safety?

Martinez and Dalot are two alterations in Man Utd’s backline, replacing Ayden Heaven and Noussair Mazraoui. Gary Neville feels the club’s defence could let them down this season.

"You can get at them" ❌Gary Neville has concerns over Manchester United's defence for the upcoming season particularly after defeat to Hull 🤔 pic.twitter.com/v3sEjInI2j

First game of the season at Old Trafford for United and one they really need to win after last weekend’s shock defeat at newly promoted Hull City.

Summer signing Andrey Santos has made way for Kobbie Mainoo to partner Youri Tielemans in attack and it’ll be really interesting to see how that midfield pairing dovetail.

It’s a first start at Old Trafford since December 2024 for Marcus Rashford in an attacking looking side. Matheus Cunha is likely to operate as a false nine.

There’s going to be an onus on Rashford and Bryan Mbeumo to provide pace and penetration from out wide and get in behind Ipswich’s defence.

Ipswich enjoyed a great start back in the top flight by winning their opening game against Sunderland and will be out to build on that victory.

Against Hull, Michael Carrick opted for a midfield pivot of Man Utd debutants Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans. However, the pair were completely overran by Hull’s intensity and energy.

Carrick has turned to Kobbie Mainoo as the resolution, with the 21-year-old replacing Andrey Santos. Mainoo went to the World Cup with England this summer, but didn’t play a single minute.

A return to Old Trafford will give Mainoo a chance to remind everyone of his quality.

"I wouldn't say massive concerns, but he will be worried""If Carrick doesn't see a reaction today, there is a problem"The Manchester United players will be under pressure to perform, says Ashley Young 📈 pic.twitter.com/dR6uat4l2P

Man Utd: Lammens, Dalot, Maguire, Martinez, Shaw, Mainoo, Tielemans, Mbeumo, Fernandes, Rashford, Cunha.

Subs: Darlow, Mazraoui, Zirkzee, Dorgu, Yoro, Santos, Heaven, Sesko, Lacey.

Ipswich: Scherpen, O’Shea, Diop, Greaves, Davis, Nunez, Lukic, Fatawu, Enciso, Maeda, Emersonn.

Subs: Walton, Furlong, Kipre, Walle, McAteer, Palacios, Akpom, Ouattara, Clarke.

Gary O’Neil has named an unchanged line-up from the side that beat Sunderland last week. Recent signing Exequiel Palacios is on the bench after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Your Town at Old Trafford! ✊ pic.twitter.com/mVMj2LVNvs

Unsurprisingly, Michael Carrick has shuffled his pack after last weekend’s disastrous defeat to Hull. Rashford, Mainoo, Martinez and Dalot all come into the starting X1.

📍 Home.Back where we belong. https://t.co/VbvwRcdF4t pic.twitter.com/37rThnGjyN

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of Sunday’s late Premier League kick-off between Manchester United and Ipswich Town at Old Trafford.

Man Utd suffered an almighty upset last weekend as they slumped to a shock 2-0 defeat against Hull City in Yorkshire. The hosts scored twice after 38 minutes, leaving Michael Carrick’s men with a mountain to climb, but they simply had no answer so Man Utd were shambolic defensively and toothless in attack.

When the fixture list was released, everyone looked at Man Utd’s opening two games against newly-promoted sides as the ideal opportunity for maximum points. But now, there is serious pressure on today’s home team to deliver in front of their fans.

Reflecting on last week’s loss in a press conference ahead of this outing, Carrick said: “I think your success comes from how well you deal with setbacks in the end. In any position, or certainly any sport, particularly this one, going through a season, there are going to be setbacks, sometimes a bit smaller than others. It’s how you deal with that initially, how you react to it and what comes next. I think that ultimately decides what type of team you’re going to become.

“So far, we’ve dealt with those setbacks really well within games and game to game. We had one last week, there’s no getting away from it, and it’s disappointing, but we’re looking to bounce back. We’ve had a good week. The boys have re-focused, learnt from where we could have improved and kept pushing forward.”

Against the odds, Ipswich began their 2026-27 Premier League campaign with a 2-1 comeback victory over Sunderland, with summer signing Emersonn equalising before substitute Jack Clarke found a 90th-minute winner at Portman Road. They followed this game with another triumph at home in midweek, beating Leicester City 3-1 in the League Cup second round.

With all eyes on Man Utd after their stuttering start, Ipswich will see this as an ideal opportunity to ruffle the feathers of a Premier League heavyweight and further dent their sky-high ambitions.

Kick-off is at 16:30, with team news coming shortly.

#1523. Costacurta criticises entire Milan squad’s mentality: “That’s a serious mistake”

Billy Costacurta has shared his thoughts on Milan’s roller coaster from the derby win to the Ferencvaros defeat, criticising the players for their mentality.

The mood took a 180-degree turn on Thursday evening as Milan failed to build on their win against Inter, losing 2-0 to Ferencvaros at San Siro. Ruben Amorim criticised the players immediately after the game, and again took to strong language at Milanello yesterday.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The manager isn’t the only one who thought they did poorly either, as our fan ratings were very low across the board. In other words, it doesn’t feel like Amorim is just shifting the blame from himself, as also highlighted by the Milan legend Costacurta.

Speaking to Gazzetta dello Sport this morning, Costacurta shared his thoughts on the difference between the derby display and the one against Ferencvaros. Above all, as he highlighted, the mentality wasn’t the right one and Milan paid the price.

Billy, how do you go from the euphoria of the derby to the tiredness of Thursday’s display against Ferencvaros?

“Having the same intensity as against Inter would have been difficult. But that’s the difference between a team that wins and one that doesn’t.”

Does this mean that the mid-week game should have been approached with the same attention as Saturday night?

“It’s normal that four days after a huge win like the one against Inter, some players think they have become stronger, and that’s a serious mistake. You think you have already reached a strong position, and it turns out to be fatal.

“You think you can do things easily, that you can always succeed, and that’s a mistake you can’t afford.”

“Musah, who lost the ball easily just a few minutes into the match. Diawara, who came out chest-first as a central defender, carrying the ball and then diving. Cisse, who insisted on receiving the ball with his feet without ever going deep, and many other details that make you think it was indeed superficial.

“I focused on these three, and that certainly doesn’t mean it was all their fault, but it was clear they didn’t enter the field with the right mentality.”

“Musah, a deputy? I wouldn’t say so. The youngsters made mistakes, yes, but not just them. In my opinion, the worst player on the pitch was Rabiot, and I’m talking about a leader, one of the best midfielders in the world.

“So, the blame is equally distributed: the lads did poorly, but so did those who should go to them and say, ‘Let’s all wake up.’ Poor technical choices can be admitted and forgiven, but the attitude, no.

“It must always be the right one and certainly never superficial. Not if you play for Milan: I say this as someone attached to the team. I repeat: you must always play as if you are playing against Inter, always trying to cause problems for the opponent. Always.”

Cisse, by the way. He didn’t celebrate your first call-up to the national team in the best way. Is he ready for it?

“I understand coach Mancini’s decisions: Roberto also tries to scout. If there’s less choice than before, you try to develop someone under your guidance.”

Is a winning mentality something that can be acquired?

“Of course, with many techniques. You can leave a player out for two games and then see if he’s understood. Or, with someone else, put him back in right away because you expect him to understand immediately.

“And then you can explain: explain that at that moment you weren’t in the right place, you didn’t have the right mentality.”

“If you have the chance to play for a team like Milan and you don’t have the desire and determination to face every match as if it were a derby, you should stay home. Or simply stay on the bench.”

“Amorim probably didn’t fully grasp the situation, otherwise why field such a team? The first half was unwatchable. It’s also true that there’s a difference between technique and attitude: perhaps the players trained well in the previous days but then completely misjudged their approach.”

On the contrary, is there an example of someone who does things right?

“I’d say Pavlovic, always alert, with the attitude everyone should have. As a starter, it might be easier to find it, but at the same time, those who have a chance should spit fire, ‘ruining’ the pitch when called upon.”

#1522. Exor pays in €60m of Juventus’ €250m raise, but UEFA deal limits January plans

Juventus shareholders have cleared a capital increase of up to €250m, and majority owner Exor has already committed €60m of it. Giovanni Carnevali warned that the UEFA settlement means nothing extraordinary should be expected in January.

Juventus shareholders gave the board the power to raise up to €250m in new capital at the Allianz Stadium on 3 November. The vote came in the extraordinary part of the meeting and passed with 99.9% in favour. The same assembly approved the 2025/26 accounts.

Part of the money is already committed. Exor has already paid in €60m as an advance towards the capital increase. That payment supports the club’s equity and finances until the board uses its new authority. The majority owner has also guaranteed its own 65.4% stake in the raise and any shares other investors leave untaken.

The squad will not see the full sum. Shoring up the club’s finances across this season and next will take 45–50% of whatever is raised, according to Football Italia. That leaves roughly €100m mainly for first-team signings before the January window. Beyond keeping equity at a suitable level, the rest will go on controlling debt and keeping the team competitive, including transfers, Corriere dello Sport reports.

The accounts show why the balance sheet needs support. The consolidated loss for 2025/26 was €66.0m. That was €7.9m bigger than the previous year’s €58.1m. The result was in line with the forecasts in the club’s half-year report to 31 December 2025. The board had approved the accounts on 29 September. Another loss is expected in 2026/27, mainly because Juventus are in the Europa League rather than the Champions League.

The assembly was Giovanni Carnevali’s first as chief executive. He promised a serious approach to the January window. His warning was just as clear. As a serious company, Juventus must honour its settlement agreement with UEFA and does not expect to do anything extraordinary.

That agreement was announced on 30 June. It is a three-year settlement with the First Chamber of UEFA’s Club Financial Control Body. It relates to Juventus breaking UEFA’s Football Earnings Rule over the three seasons from 2022/23 to 2024/25.

For supporters, the message is mixed. The capital increase gives the club fresh resources. The settlement still dictates how quickly that money can be used on the pitch.

Shareholders also criticised the club for keeping a low profile in recent years. President Gianluca Ferrero declared Juventus open to dialogue with Tether.

The terms of the UEFA deal leave little margin. Missing the targets agreed with UEFA for the current season or the next two can lead to limits on the club’s UEFA List A and further sporting sanctions. The settlement runs until the 2027/28 financial year.

#1520. Press not dealt with and unexploited spaces: Tactical analysis of AC Milan 0-2 Ferencvaros

AC Milan suffered a disappointing defeat against Ferencvaros on Thursday evening, and as highlighted in our tactical analysis, a lot went wrong for the Rossoneri.

Milan’s Europa League campaign has turned into somewhat of a nightmare, after being tipped to fight for the title in the summer. Just one win in the first four games means a top 8 finish is very difficult, while there are no guarantees for the playoffs either.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ruben Amorim certainly voiced his disappointment after the game, sending a clear message to the players, even if the head coach deserves some of the blame too. Below is the tactical breakdown from Rohit Rajeev, who has pointed out several flaws.

Ferencvaros were committed to pressing Milan and looked to create numerical overloads in the wide spaces. In this particular sequence, Milan found themselves in a 6v8 situation, highlighting the numerical disadvantage they faced when trying to play out from the back.

In the centre, Musah was very isolated as Bartesaghi, Cisse and Hutchinson failed to drop short or move inside to make themselves available. This left the American with limited options and made it easier for Ferencvaros to sustain their press and disrupt Milan’s build-up.

Individual errors also made things difficult for Milan when going forward. In the example below, Terracciano failed to play a simple pass into Hutchinson’s path, preventing Milan from launching a counter-attack.

As Ferencvaros were pressing high and maintained a high defensive line as a result, there was space to exploit in behind. However, Milan failed to make runs behind the defence, while very few long balls were played to target that space.

The lack of depth in their attacking movements allowed Ferencvaros to remain compact, leaving little room between the lines for Milan to exploit. It also meant that Ramos was very isolated up front, with effectively a 3v1 created against him.

The first goal that Milan conceded stemmed from two individual errors. De Winter made a poor decision by playing the ball back to Torriani, while the goalkeeper’s heavy first touch didn’t exactly make things any better in stopping the danger.

Milan then pushed forward in search of an equaliser and their defence was reduced from three players to two. Ferencvaros won possession after De Winter’s clearance, launching a quick counter-attack.

Joseph then made an intelligent run to block Bartesaghi’s path, preventing him from recovering defensively.

Taking a look at Milan’s first half, it was characterised by sterile possession as there were significantly more passes in their own half as opposed to the opponent’s half. Ferencvaros also dominated the physical battles, winning every ground duel and breaking up any attacking rhythm for Milan.
