Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1505. Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer speaks out to reveal his 'enormous pain' and says he will 'face whatever comes' after police opened homicide investigation and fans called him 'murderer'

Published: 11:22 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 13:47 EDT, 4 November 2026

Jesus Owono, the goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision with the late Jesus de Miguel, has spoken for the first time since the tragic incident.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker de Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw with Tenerife in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Owono has since shut down his Instagram account amid the significant backlash he has received – which saw him subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans as he left the pitch – but he has now issued a statement alongside his club.

'FC Andorra continues to be deeply affected by the death of Jesús de Miguel,' they wrote. 'In these very difficult moments, our player Jesús Owono wishes to personally share a few words.'

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Jesus Owono has broken his silence after being involved in a fatal collision with Jesus de Miguel

Tenerife striker de Miguel died on Tuesday morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

The club added: 'FC Andorra asks for the utmost sensitivity and respect.'

Andorra held a minute's silence at the club's training ground today, and the collision has opened the debate surrounding challenges involving goalkeepers and outfield players in football.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected' by the tragedy.

'There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,' Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

'What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

'First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch.'

Spatz continued: 'I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

'In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating de Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Police are investigating the death of de Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died on Tuesday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

#1504. The Mbappé-Yamal duel panics Europe, the German press worries about Kompany

It’s Clasico day! This Sunday, Barça hosts Real Madrid at the Camp Nou for a “Classico in gold“, as written by almost the entire Spanish press. Beyond the clash between the country’s two big names, it is the duel between Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappé that stands out. Already, the two stars are always in the news, especially when there is a Clasico and even more so on the eve of the Ballon d’Or. The newspaper A.S. also titled in the same way, which shows the impact of this duel in this shock. On the one hand, Lamine Yamal wants to crush his rival and draw an almost definitive line on La Liga while the season has just started, hoping to triumph tomorrow evening in London. On the other hand, Kylian Mbappé wants to reconnect with Barça, shine at Camp Nou and also wants to win the Ballon d’Or tomorrow evening. Even in France, the subject is the same. “Two talents, one summit”, writes the newspaper The Team. Stats-wise, Lamine Yamal has not scored in the last two Clasicos, unlike Kylian Mbappé who often hits the mark in this type of match. And yet, almost every time, it is the Barcelonan who emerges victorious.

The state of health of Vincent Kompany still worries Bayern Munich. The Belgian technician had health problems recently, until Friday and felt unwell during Bayern Munich training. He was rushed to hospital where his condition was stabilized. This incident would not be surprising in the eyes of his professional entourage. For several weeks, members of the club had been worried about his pace of life and his very intense investment in his job. In addition, he had been suffering from a viral infection for several days. At Bayern Munich, some were concerned about his lack of sleep, his questionable diet and especially his excessive consumption of coffee to stay awake. In addition to all that, Kompany would have abandoned physical activities, while accumulating working hours without giving himself any rest. Club leaders visited him several times in the Munich clinic where he is hospitalized, including Uli Hoeneß. The honorary president of Bayern wanted to personally show his support. Sports director Max Eberl explained that Kompany should be able to recover without pressure: “ It’s Bayern Munich. These are not nice words. We are a family, and we are here to support each other and get through this together. » In the meantime, Vincent Kompany will be replaced by his deputy, Aaron Danks.

RC Lens and Florian Thauvin sing in the rain. Whether it’s windy, rainy or sunny, it’s impossible to be bitter among the Sang et Or as long as Thauvin is there. Manhandled against Paris FC at home, RC Lens once again relied on their captain and won 2-1 thanks to a goal and an assist from the former Marseille player. For his 300th Ligue 1 match, Florian Thauvin confirmed his sparkling form from the start of the season, a few days after starting on the bench in the Champions League to take a breather. But the Lensois are dependent on Thauvin and we saw it again last night. The French international was well helped by Thorgan Hazard, also the author of a goal and an assist after coming into play. For his part, Florian Thauvin once again spoke of the France team, a goal that he has not lost sight of. “ As a competitor, my goal is to go there, but it’s not my place to claim. I have to give myself every chance. Today, I demonstrate every weekend that I am performing well, but then, we trust our legend, our coach “, declared Florian Thauvin.

You all know, tonight is the big night. The 70th Ballon d’Or ceremony in history takes place this Monday in London and the suspense remains total. This is also the opinion of most European media. “The most undecided Ballon d’Or in history”explain Le Figarowhich attempts to find a favorite by highlighting the three criteria. Same atmosphere at Parisian : “tight as ever”. The Ile-de-France newspaper would obviously like to see a PSG player triumph for the second time in a row, after Ousmane Dembélé. The big favorites are Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal. In their own way, they have marked this football season, with their goals for the first two and with his magic for the last, but also with his record and his World Cup. #1497. The dirtiest football match EVER: Referee issues record 51 RED CARDS after mass brawl in Under-20 game in Brazil - and even the ball boys got involved!

Published: 14:28 EDT, 4 November 2026 | Updated: 14:56 EDT, 4 November 2026

A world record 51 red cards were shown in one game during an Under-20 match in Brazil following a mass brawl.

The Guinness Book of World Records has confirmed that the game saw the most dismissals ever, with 43 players and eight members of coaching staff given their marching orders.

Said record came after the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship clash between Uberlandia and Mamore descended into chaos following an altercation near the technical areas.

Uberlandia had initially been reduced to ten men after Luike Bispo dos Santos struck an opposing player in the stomach.

In the 54th minute of the game, nearly four football teams' worth of players were involved in an incident that saw some players chasing others, with military police called to the stadium.

The referee reported that six ball boys were also involved, and threw punches, kicks and objects at players and coaching staff.

GUINNESS WORLD RECORD HAS BEEN BROKEN IN BRAZIL IN A FOOTBALL GAME. A Guinness World Record was broken for the number of red cards in a single game, the Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship clash between Uberlândia and Mamoré saw 51 sendings off, including 43 players and eight… pic.twitter.com/UuBZ4oqhiC

A record 51 players were shown a red card amid a mass brawl during a Brazilian match

Weapons were also said to have been used, including stretchers and chairs. The chaos took well over half an hour to cool.

The previous record was 36 red cards, achieved after a brawl in an Argentine fifth division game between Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in 2011.

According to Brazilian outlet Ge Globo, Uberlandia manager Willer Francisco Silva ran onto the field to confront referee Fernando Patrick with two other members of his coaching staff.

It is reported that threats of violence were given.

The game was eventually re-started, before the fourth goal of the game, which put Uberlandia down, triggered the brawl.

In total, 22 players from Uberlandia and 21 from their opponents were sent off, as well as four members of staff from each side.

#1495. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

Cody Gakpo was linked with both Tottenham and Manchester City during the transfer window but stayed at Liverpool and has been in good form in these first three games of the season. He has assisted all three of Alexander Isak’s goals so far.

4 - Cody Gakpo has been directly involved in four goals in the Premier League this season (1 goal, 3 assists). This century, only Mo Salah in 2024-25 has had more goal involvements through Liverpool's opening three games of a league campaign (6).Retained. pic.twitter.com/hGN0NpF5A3

"He's important for us"Virgil van Dijk says Cody Gakpo will be important for Liverpool this season after the win over Ipswich 💪 pic.twitter.com/XLWfxbpK2d

“You have to believe in yourself and have the belief of the fans that you are the man when you come for that much money. He had a terrible injury last year, but you can hear the Liverpool fans. They absolutely love what they saw. Some of his skills, his movement. That comes from his goal last week and the confidence that brings. Fingers crossed he can carry this on.”

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Andoni Iraola is bringing on Nyoni for Mac Allister, who was on a booking.

Davis is found making a run in behind and his cross from the left side of the box is blocked by Araujo and goes behind for a corner. Lukic’s delivery is headed away at the front post by Gravenberch.

Double change for Ipswich as McAteer and Ouattara replace Fatawau and Palacios.

Barcola drives down Liverpool’s left and, as he approaches the Ipswich box, cuts onto his right and feeds it across to Gakpo, whose shot misses the target.

The ball comes to Flemming on the edge of the box and he tries to curl one into the far corner but it is an easy save for Alisson.

Barcola is nearly played in behind but Scherpen does really to get out of his goal quickly and gets to the ball first, just ahead of Barcola.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

#IPSLIV – 68'VAR recommended an on-field review for a potential penalty, but determined that Szoboszlai was in an offside position in the build-up.REF: "After review, there's a penalty shout on Szoboszlai. However, in the build-up to the penalty shout, Szoboszlai is in an… pic.twitter.com/DN4i8rj5fg

Liverpool are demanding a penalty. Szoboszlai is played in behind and is constantly having his shirt pulled by Davis. Davis then appears to bring Szoboszlai down inside the box but the referee waves it away. Davis gets none of the ball and the referee is being sent to the screen...

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Possession: Ipswich 41%-59% LiverpoolShots: 8-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 3-2Touches in opposition box: 7-12

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel at Portman Road and we are moments away from kick-off. Here is a reminder of how the two sides line up this evening:

The Paraguayan is in his second stint at Ipswich and has two assists to his name in the first two league games.

“It gives us a big belief that we can compete at the level. Coming up from the Championship, there is always some doubt around. The home win over Sunderland was huge for us. And then to be in the game for as long as we were at Manchester United was impressive. I have challenged the lads a lot. We do not focus on the outcome or results, we just commit to being the best version of ourselves. We cannot go toe-to-toe with everyone. We have to be sensible and smart.”

Andoni Iraola has made a change at right-back tonight, with Ronaldu Araujo replacing Jeremie Frimpong. Araujo arrived at Liverpool this summer on loan with an option to buy from Barcelona.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1494. PSG: former Titi Oumar Camara reveals the reasons for his departure

19-year-old left winger, Oumar Camara is performing well in Portugal. The Vitória Guimarães player has 7 goals and 3 assists in 46 matches since his arrival in the summer of 2025. The native of Aubervilliers quickly reached a milestone after being trained at Paris Saint-Germain. A club where he didn’t really have any prospects, as he confided to The Team : “playing time in the first team. And then the confidence, the certainty that it is a springboard club. In 2024, at PSG, the Espoirs group was not yet something consolidated. I had just completed two seasons in U19. I had the feeling of having validated this first step and of not having the prospect of going higher. »

Winner of the Portuguese League Cup with Vitória Guimarães and with regularity, he found an easier context in which to flourish than within the Ile-de-France club. According to him, it remains difficult for a young person trained at PSG to have a chance: “It really depends on the case. But I perceived the project as vague. They tell you that you’re going to start again with the pros, but after that, what happens? Will there be continuity? Are we going to go back down? I also think that quite a few generations were held back by the elimination of the reserve team (in 2019). There is a luck factor, too. Quentin Ndjantou, last year, he scored a hat-trick in the Youth League, there were injuries in the first team, and he is progressing. He played a little. The most important thing is to string together the minutes. At our ages, that’s the main thing. And here in Vitória, I do it. If I had to make this choice again, I would 1000% do it again. »

#1493. Kone excluded from France squad, to be called up vs Sassuolo

The Frenchman, forced to be substituted after just 17 minutes against Real Madrid, sees the light at the end of the tunnel.

Tonight – November 7 – he’ll return to the bench at the Olimpico, but he’s unlikely to be seen on the pitch except for a brief stint.

The number 17 has been sidelined for more than 20 days with a thigh flexor injury.

#1492. Manchester United’s nine original ‘Fergie’s Fledglings’ & how they fared

While everyone remembers Manchester United‘s iconic Class of ’92, they weren’t the first group of young players that Sir Alex Ferguson worked with at Old Trafford.

Ferguson had some talented young players on his books in the late 1980s and they were the first group to be dubbed ‘Fergie’s Fledglings’ by the press.

We’ve taken a look back at Ferguson’s first batch of fledglings to see how they all fared.

After winning United’s Young Player of the Year award in 1987-88, Martin replaced Arthur Albiston and became their first-choice left-back over the following two seasons.

He only scored two goals for the club but one of them was the winner in the 1990 FA Cup final replay against Crystal Palace as Ferguson secured his first trophy at United.

But the defender struggled with injury problems after that FA Cup final win while Clayton Blackmore and Denis Irwin established themselves as United’s first-choice full-back pairing.

Martin was sold to Celtic in January 1994 and then had a spell at Bristol Rovers before seeing out his playing career in non-league football.

“If you’d told me at 16 I would play 110 games [for United] and score the winner in the FA Cup final I’d have snapped your hand off,” Martin told the Sun.

“I was a United fan, I still am, and it was just a great time. We all felt it was the start of a new team and to play my part in it is something I’m so proud of.”

Lee Martin scored in the #FACupFinal replay against Crystal Palace to secure Sir Alex Ferguson his first trophy as Manchester United manager. pic.twitter.com/dKaXvzuNX7

— Cantona Collars AKA Larry (@Cantona_Collars) May 17, 2021

Gill was handed his first-team debut early in Ferguson’s reign, filling in for the injured Bryan Robson during a 1-1 draw away against Southampton in January 1987.

“I’d never played in central midfield at United before so it was a surprise and I imagine very much a gamble for the manager,” Gill told Retro United.

“I was wearing Bryan Robson’s No.7 shirt and just so happened to wear New Balance boots at the time so I got a bit of stick in the dressing room along the lines of who did I think I was.”

But an Achilles tendon injury derailed Gill’s progress, keeping him on the sidelines throughout the 1987-98 season.

He started to become a first-team regular in 1988-89, only to suffer a broken leg and a shattered ankle during a game against Nottingham Forest in March 1989. Gill tried to recover but never played professional football again, retiring at the age of 22.

Ferguson wrote in 1992 that he would “undoubtedly have made it” if it wasn’t for injuries.

Alongside Martin and Gill, Wilson was part of the youth team that reached the 1986 FA Youth Cup final, but he made just six substitute appearances for United’s first team.

After loan spells at Lincoln City and Charlton Athletic, the midfielder was released by United at the end of the 1990-91 season.

He spent the next two seasons with Bristol Rovers before moving abroad, playing for teams in Finland and Sweden until his retirement in 2006.

Beardsmore made an immediate impact in United’s first team, registering a goal and two assists in a 3-1 win against Liverpool on just his second league start for the club.

He made a total of 73 appearances for the Red Devils but failed to live up to the initial hype and that Liverpool game ultimately proved to be the zenith of his United career.

The winger wasn’t named in the matchday squad for the 1990 FA Cup final or the 1991 European Cup Winners’ Cup final and failed to make a single Premier League appearance in 1992-93.

He joined Bournemouth on a free transfer in 1993 and made over 200 appearances during his five years at the club before a back injury forced him to retire at the age of 29.

Fergie's first fledglings of Lee Sharpe, Mark Robins and Russell Beardsmore combine to make it 3-1 against Liverpool on New Year's Day 1989

A lovely jinking run on the left by Sharpe and a wonderful volley from Russell Beardsmore past Mike Hooper #MUFC pic.twitter.com/miLt5BnSaD

— 80s&90sFootball ⚽ (@80s90sfootball) March 28, 2022

United fought off interest from Tottenham, Chelsea and Manchester City to sign a 17-year-old Brazil from Irish side Rivermount Boys in March 1986.

The right-back later became captain of United’s reserves but made just two cameo appearances for the first team before going on loan to Oldham Athletic and Swansea City.

“We were all looking over our shoulders at the Class of ’92 because we’d go and watch them play,” he told the 42. “They were only Under-16s, maybe, at the time but you’d sit there and watch and think, ‘Who are these boys?’ So we knew that was coming.

“And I think Fergie knew too and he almost used us as a template in many ways. A lot of us left because of the likes of those boys coming through.”

After spotting Gary Neville’s progress, he decided to join Cardiff City on a permanent deal in 1992 and went on to make over 100 appearances for the club.

Robins scored 17 goals in 70 first-team appearances for United, including the winner in an FA Cup third-round tie at Nottingham Forest which reportedly saved Ferguson’s job.

“I had no idea that goal against Nottingham Forest would become so important in the history of Manchester United,” Robins would later reflect in an interview with The Telegraph. “How could I at the time? Nobody knew it was a pivotal moment for Sir Alex Ferguson.”

But the striker failed to usurp Mark Hughes and Brian McClair and was deemed surplus to requirements following Dion Dublin’s arrival in the summer of 1992.

After joining Norwich City, he scored two goals in a 4-2 win against Arsenal on the opening day of the inaugural Premier League season and was also part of the side which famously defeated Bayern Munich in the UEFA Cup.

The 52-year-old left the Canaries in 1995 and then embarked on a nomadic career, playing for 11 different clubs over the following 10 years before hanging up his boots.

Despite being a prolific goalscorer in the youth teams, Graham made just four first-team appearances for United and scored his solitary goal for the club in an FA Cup tie against QPR.

The striker completed a £50,000 move to Barnsley in August 1991 but failed to make much of an impact at Oakwell, scoring just two goals in 42 appearances.

Short spells at Preston, Carlisle United, Stockport County, Scunthorpe and Halifax Town followed before he dropped into non-league football.

Unlike the Class of ’92, Fergie’s original fledglings didn’t just feature United academy graduates. Sharpe started his career at Torquay United before moving to Old Trafford shortly after his 17th birthday.

The winger quickly became a fan favourite at United due to his flair and won the PFA Young Player of the Year award in 1990-91 but was later usurped by the emerging Ryan Giggs,

While he didn’t live up to his potential, Sharpe still won three Premier League titles, two FA Cups, the League Cup and European Cup Winners’ Cup. He also won eight England caps, making him the only player on this list to have represented their national team at senior level.

Leeds United spent a club-record £4.5million on Sharpe in 1996, but he struggled with a series of injury problems and played just 35 times in three years, scoring six goals.

The 51-year-old later had stints at Bradford City, Portsmouth, Exeter City and Icelandic side Grindavik before retiring at Garforth Town.

Maiorana joined United from Eastern Counties League side Histon in a £30,000 deal after initially going on trial and impressing Ferguson in a friendly game against Birmingham City in 1988.

The winger showed glimpses of his raw talent during eight first-team appearances, but he had a turbulent relationship with the manager and was banished to the reserves.

“[Alex Ferguson] used to belittle me in front of people,” he told FourFourTwo. “Darren Ferguson would have his head in his hands, just shaking his head.

“Once, I went up to him and said, ‘What the f*ck has your dad got against me? What have I done to him?’ He didn’t know what to say. He was embarrassed. That happened on numerous occasions.”

After picking up a knee injury in a reserve game in 1991, he would only play five more first-team games in his entire career and they all came for Ljungskile SK in the Swedish second tier.

#1491. Gollini remains sidelined, Vasquez to replace him

Roma lost at Old Trafford, but Devis Vasquez put in a solid performance and did his best to counter Man United’s late push.

The Colombian, who returned to the national team after several years, will have to repeat his performance at the Olimpico.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Pierluigi Gollini is not fit for tonight’s match, November 7th, against Sassuolo.

The 1998-born player, who until a few months ago was out of the squad, will return to Serie A 17 months and 13 days after his last appearance (Empoli-Verona, May 25, 2025).

#1490. Cristiano Ronaldo: 9 of his international records that will never be broken

Cristiano Ronaldo has called time on his incredible international career with Portugal and will leave behind a legacy hard to match.

Ronaldo is bowing out from international duty after 234 caps and 146 goals for Portugal. He won the Euros with them in 2016 and went on to triumph twice in the UEFA Nations League.

A World Cup evaded him, but Ronaldo made his mark at that competition too over the years, scoring 11 times across six tournaments.

As one of the best players in history, his efforts in a Portugal shirt will stand the test of time in the record books.

He boasts plenty of records in international football – and these ones might never be beaten.

There are only three men with more than 100 international goals, but Ronaldo is way out in front. He quits 20 ahead of Lionel Messi, who also retired from international football this year, and 38 ahead of Ali Daei.

The active footballer closest to Ronaldo’s record is Romelu Lukaku on 94, but at the age of 33, it’s hard to see him catching up. The same goes for 38-year-old Robert Lewandowski on 92.

We’re pretty sure Harry Kane has plenty more goals for England in the tank, but enough to overtake Ronaldo? He’d need more than 50, so it’s a long shot.

If anyone stands half a chance it’s probably Erling Haaland on 65 goals, but his chances might depend on how many major tournaments Norway qualify for. It’s easy to forget the 2026 World Cup was their first major tournament since Euro 2000.

There’s Kylian Mbappe on 67 for France as well, but it makes you realise how impressive Ronaldo’s record is when you consider he’s not even halfway to reaching it.

Ronaldo has been able to reach those lofty goalscoring heights by playing more than anyone else in the international game.

His 234 caps for Portugal are 26 more than the amount Messi managed for Argentina. Third on the list is the still-active Luka Modric, 28 behind his former Real Madrid teammate but nearing the end at the age of 41.

Qatar’s Hassan Al-Haydos is the next nearest active challenger on 193 caps. The Al Sadd captain is only 35, so might end up not too far off, but it’ll still be a tall order.

Ronaldo played for his country for 23 years, after all, and that longevity is going to be hard for anyone to match.

Talking of longevity, Ronaldo hasn’t been wasting time at the tail end of his career. He actually scored nearly twice as many goals for Portugal after turning 30 than before.

It probably makes sense, with Ronaldo playing more centrally as the years went on after starting out as a winger.

In total, he scored 94 goals for Portugal after turning 30, compared to 52 before.

Unsurprisingly, it’s Messi behind him in the ranking, with an impressive 68 goals for Argentina after his 30th birthday.

But Ronaldo’s record will take some beating. Only four other players have ever scored 94 international goals, let alone after the age of 30. This one’s probably sticking.

Similar principle here. Ronaldo scored in 96 of the Portugal games he played in. Only he, Messi and Daei have reached that amount of goals in international football regardless of whether they were scoring braces or hat-tricks.

Ronaldo scored against a grand total of 49 different countries for Portugal, meaning he had three more victims on the international stage than Messi.

An ever-expanding World Cup might help, but it’s hard to imagine anyone scoring against 50 different countries.

It’d probably have to be someone from Europe or Africa, since those confederations have the most members. But they’d still be relying on the luck of the draw in qualifiers for tournaments.

Ronaldo scored for Portugal in 23 different years, which is longer than most players’ international careers – let alone for them to be consistently delivering in front of goal.

Even if a player was to make their international debut at 18, they’d have to play into their forties and score without fail every year to surpass Ronaldo’s record.

Ronaldo might have missed out on the all-time World Cup scoring record, but he does boast the most goals at European Championships.

His final tally of 14 is five higher than the next best, Michel Platini on nine.

Alvaro Morata and Kane have seven each, but will be 35 and 34 by the time the next Euros start. Kane could give him a run for his money, but he might only have one more shot at it. If the next Euros are his last, he’d need to score eight times to beat Ronaldo’s record – something only Platini has done at a single Euros tournament before.

Ronaldo is one of only two outfield players to make more than 20 Euros appearances, so if anyone wants to threaten his goalscoring record, their ratio is going to have to be high.

As stated, Ronaldo played in 30 Euros matches. It only takes seven games to go from the group stage all the way to the final, so someone would have to do that four times and more to beat his record.

UEFA have previously put plans to expand the Euros on the backburner, so someone would need to have a near-20-year international career – and do well in it – to come close to Ronaldo’s record.

Ronaldo and Messi are the only outfield players to go to six World Cups – and Ronaldo scored at every one he went to.

Unless the World Cup becomes a more frequent event than one that happens every four years, someone would have to play for two decades, always qualify for the World Cup and always score at it to match Ronaldo’s record, let alone beat it.

#1488. What would the Premier League table look like if Man City get kicked out?

While Manchester City’s future is up in the air, one real possibility is that they could be expelled from the Premier League this season.

Some reports suggest City’s Premier League rivals are keen for any punishment to be dished out before the end of the current campaign and while that could be anything from a fine to a transfer ban to a points deduction, it is not out of the realm of possibility that City are kicked out of the league entirely.

Expulsion from a league is not without precedent. Both Bury and Maidstone United were kicked out of the Football League due to financial reasons but, crucially, had not played a match that season.

It would, though, be unheard of in Premier League history and would have a knock-on effect for all other 19 clubs, not to mention the ones who have already played City.

If City are expelled during the season, the most likely outcome is that their results would be expunged from the record. How different would that make the current Premier League table look?

If City were expelled during the season, Premier League Rule C.15 states that their results would be expunged from the league table and the number of relegation places reduced by one. However, if they were expelled after the season had concluded, C.15 would not apply in the same way, meaning their completed results would not automatically be wiped from the table.

City had won their first seven Premier League games, meaning none of their rivals would have lost any points from the hypothetical expulsion.

But losses to Aston Villa and Brighton change things slightly. They’d be the only team to lose three points, having become the first side to take anything off City this season.

The obvious place to start then is that every team would move up one spot due to City currently being top of the table.

That would put Arsenal top with 21 points from eight matches, five clear of Brighton in second. Chelsea would be third, albeit with a game in hand.

At the other end, Crystal Palace, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland would occupy the bottom three, although the reduction in relegation places would mean only Forest and Sunderland would be going down.

As for the goals, Sunderland would be happy to see five wiped off their conceded tally although would lose three of their own. Liverpool and Ipswich would see three goals wiped off too.

It would be win-win for United and Coventry who would have one taken off their conceded without anything happening to their scored column.

Bournemouth and Palace both scored one in their defeats to City so would also be up overall in terms of goal difference.

Brighton would boast the best goal difference in the division at +16, having scored an impressive 23 goals in their eight matches against the other 18 clubs.

Here’s how the 2026-27 table shapes up if you expunge City’s results from the record.

Type in your first guess then hit enter. Each tile will change colour to indicate if the letter is in the correct position, elsewhere in the word or does not appear at all. A green tile means the letter is in the correct position; an orange tile means the letter is elsewhere in the word; a grey tile means that letter is not in the word at all.

If you are struggling, you will see a hint button that becomes available from your fourth attempt. Clicking it will reveal a tile, though note this is only available to logged-in users.

You can also click Give Up if you’re really struggling and just want to be put out of your misery. It’s not one for the purists, but it’s nice to have the option!

#1484. The 6 players Arsenal let go in the summer – & how they’re faring elsewhere

Arsenal sold six members of their squad permanently in the summer and we’ve tracked down what they have been up to.

After winning the title, the Gunners had a small squad rejuvenation but it was more out than in as Mikel Arteta showed his ruthless streak.

Here are those six players and how they have got on at their new clubs so far.

Before Martinelli, Arsenal were incredibly low in terms of their record sale but his big-money move to Saudi netted them £55.7m.

The Brazilian went off to Al-Hilal to join the likes of Ruben Neves, Kalidou Koulibaly, Theo Hernandez and latterly Ollie Watkins and the former Arsenal winger has hit the ground running for his new club.

Martinelli has got six in six so far for his new side and has scored in the last four matches he has played in, one of which was a 54-minute hat-trick.

Al-Hilal are currently top and Martinelli is only 25, so we could see him back in Europe at some point.

Before they sold Martinelli, Arsenal got rid of more of their left-wing depth by allowing Trossard to go.

No one would really begrudge them that decision. He was 31 and had already proven his worth for the £27m they paid for him back in 2023.

Arsenal made a good chunk of that back when he joined Besiktas for an initial £15.4m.

Since moving to Turkey, the Belgian has made a good start, although he has had a few injuries to deal with.

It took him four games to register his first Super Lig goal, but he followed up that assist with a goal in a 3-0 win over Erzurumspor.

A heel injury disrupted his rhythm, but he was back amongst the goals last time out when he scored in a 2-2 draw away at Kasimpasa.

Besiktas are fourth in the Super Lig, which is quickly becoming the Premier League’s retirement home.

After failing to break into Arsenal’s back line, Kiwior moved to Porto for the low price of £14.7 million.

That is already looking a bit of a bargain for the Portuguese club as he has played every minute of their Liga Portugal campaign so far.

Francesco Farioli’s Porto have won all 10 league games they had faced and Kiwior has been part of a defence that has conceded just four goals, easily the best of any team in the division.

Unsurprisingly, they lead the Liga Portugal and already have a five-point gap over second-place Benfica.

In one of the best examples of falling upwards of all time, Jesus went from the bench at Arsenal to Barcelona.

He is playing a similar role in Catalonia with just two of his seven La Liga games having been starts but when he has played, he’s done well.

He’s got three goals and one assist in the league and has been an able deputy for the free-scoring Raphinha.

It had been over two years since Vieira actually played for Arsenal, but his association with the club is finally over.

The two parted ways permanently in the summer following two loan spells to Porto and Hamburg.

He joined the latter permanently in the summer, but they are struggling so far this season and sit 15th of the 18-team Bundesliga.

Vieira has not helped with those struggles. In 333 minutes of action, he has yet to score or assist and has not lived up to the £8.6m the German club paid for him.

One of the stranger Arsenal signings in recent years was Brentford captain Norgaard, who was brought in for depth and then never played.

He played 20 games across the entire season and a year later was gone. Everton and David Moyes took him on, but he has yet to make much of an impact.

He missed the first five Premier League games with a groin injury and has so far only played five minutes in a 2-0 defeat at home to Chelsea.

He has had minimal cup action too, having played just four minutes against Newcastle in the League Cup round of 16.

The Dane looks back at full fitness now, so we will wait and see whether Moyes plays him more than Arteta did.
